name: GERDA
summary: GERDA was an enriched-germanium double-beta-decay experiment at LNGS. Its low-background energy spectrum also supports searches for direct absorption of bosonic dark matter and dark Compton scattering.
detection_principle: Bare germanium detectors operate in liquid argon. Liquid-argon scintillation anticoincidence and germanium spectroscopy suppress backgrounds; full dark-matter energy deposition can produce a narrow peak.

status.label: Completed
status.evidence: The GERDA website states that data taking stopped in February 2020. Main Phase-II data extend chiefly through December 2019, followed by continued analysis of historical data.

timeline.event: All data taking stops, according to the website

results.summary: No bosonic-dark-matter signal above background was found; direct-absorption and dark-Compton channels were constrained.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
